caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No.115 of 2013.
lawyer:
Abdullah-al-Mamun, Advocate instructed bit Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record --- For the Petitioners. 
Shafique Ahmed, Senior Advocate instructed by Md Taufique Hossain, Advocate-on-Record --- For the Respondents.
parties:
Parul Nath and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
State ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Md Abdul Wahhab Miah J: This Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal has been filed by the petitioners against the judgment and order dated the 10th day of December, 2012 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 46490 of 2012 summarily rejecting an application filed by them under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure (the Code). 

 2. Facts giving rise to this petition are that on 11-8-2004, the District Task Force, Chittagong, on a secret information, raided the Jewellery shop known as "Nath Jewellers" owned by Sree Ram Krishna Nath alias Ram Babu (the deceased husband and father respectively of the present petitioners) at Khatungonj, Boxirhat, Chittagong and seized gold ornaments weighing 104 kgs, 4 tolas and 4½ ratis silver ornaments weighing 3kgs, 500 grams and stones worth Taka 5455 used in ornaments and, in addition, also recovered a sum of Taka 24,18,085. First Information Report (FIR) was lodged with Kotwali Police Station on 12-8-2004, giving rise to Kotwali Police Station Case No. 24(8)2004 under section 25B of the Special Powers Act, 1974 (the Act, 1974). The informant deposited the seized alamots, namely: gold and silver ornaments, cash money and stone with Bangladesh Bank, Chittagong. Accused-Sree Ram Krishna Nath surrendered before the High Court Division and obtained anticipatory bail and also submitted an application for return of the seized ornaments and money as well as other articles recovered from his shop. 46 (forty six) other persons as claimants also filed applications for returning of the seized alamots to them. 

 3. During investigation, 5(five) Registers for the years 1407-1411 BS had been seized as alamots containing the description of the gold ornaments and the amount of money payable by the clients including those 46 persons and the other mortgagors. On conclusion of investigation, the Police submitted a final report on 22-4-2005 stating that the principal accused-Ram Krishna Nath was an established businessman, a pawn broker, lending money by taking gold ornaments as security. His ancestors had been engaged in the same business in the selfsame premises. The informant did not file any naraji petition against the said final report. An offence under the Act, 1974 being exclusively cognizable by a Special Tribunal, final report was sent to the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Chittagong, ex-officio Metropolitan Special Tribunal No. 1, Chittagong (hereinafter referred to as the Tribunal) for necessary action. The case was registered as Special Tribunal Case No. 108 of 2005. The Tribunal by its order dated 15-5-2005 accepted the final report and discharged the accused from the case with a direction upon the concerned authority to return the seized gold, silver ornaments, money and the other articles to the principal accused, Ram Krishna Nath alias Ram Babu. The Tribunal further directed Ram Krishna Nath to return the seized gold ornaments to the other claimants who deposited those with him as per seized Registers and report compliance thereof to it within 1(one) month. The Tribunal also directed the concerned Jimmader to return the seized articles given in his jimma to accused-Ram Krishna Nath. The Tribunal sent the copy of the order to the Officer-in-charge, Kotwali Police Station, Chittagong Metropolitan Police and the Manager, Bangladesh Bank for information and for taking necessary steps. Thereafter, on 7-6-2005, the informant filed an application before the Tribunal for further investigation. 

 4. The same informant, Subedar Md. Harun Mia also lodged a second FIR on 7-6-2005 on the selfsame allegation against the same accused under section 13 of the মানিলন্ডারিং প্রতিরোধ আইন, ২০০২ (the Act, 2002) whereupon Kotwali Police Station Case No.  16(6)2005 was started. The case was registered as GR Case No. 393 of 2005 (hereinafter referred to as GR Case No. 393 of 2005). On the prayer of the Investigation Officer made on 9-6-2005 alamots seized in Kotwali Police Station Case No.  24(8)2004 under section 25B of the Act, 1974 (GR number of this PS Case is not available from the record) were also shown as alamots in connection with Kotwali Police Station Case No.  16(6)2005 under section 13 of the Act, 2002 by the order of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong. In the meantime, the Tribunal by its order dated 13-6-2005 rejected the prayer for further investigation on the finding that on acceptance of the final report submitted in Kotwali Police Station Case No.  24(8)2004, it ceased to have any jurisdiction to pass any order for further investigation. On conclusion of investigation of the subsequent case (GR Case No. 393 of 2005), the Police submitted charge-sheet on 30-9-2005 under section 13 of the Ain, 2002. Accused-Sree Ram Krishna Nath then preferred an application under section 561A of the Code before the High Court Division seeking quashment of the proceedings of GR Case No. 393 of 2005. The Rule was issued upon the State and another to show cause as to why the proceedings of the said GR case should not be quashed and it was registered as Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 4296 of 2006. By the judgment and order dated 30-1-2008, the High Court Division made the Rule absolute and quashed the proceedings and gave the following directions: 

 "The informant is directed to return the original Receipts of safe deposit of the seized articles and the money deposited with Bangladesh Bank to the accused petitioner of the case. The Commander of 43 Rifle Battalion, Halisahar, Chittagong as the recipient of original receipt of Bangladesh Bank in respect of seized articles, is directed to ensure return of original Safe Deposit Annexure-C1-C4 to the Joint Manager, Banking (Bangladesh Bank), Chittagong Branch Opposite Party No. 2 herein. 

 6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 4296 of 2006 quashing the proceedings of GR Case No. 393 of 2005, the State preferred Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal before this Court and leave having been granted gave rise to Criminal Appeal No. 43 of 2009. The appeal was dismissed by this Court on 12-10-2011. However, during the course of hearing of the appeal, this Court was informed that by the time, the principal accused (Ram Krishna Nath) died, the direction of the High Court Division to return the seized articles to 46 (forty six) claimants was modified as under: 

 11. Therefore, the gold ornaments which are now lying in the custody of Bangladesh Bank in open and unpacked condition without the name and serial number of mortgage "to which Sree Ram Krishna Nath was the rightful owner should be returned to the petitioners who are rightful claimants being the legal heirs and successors of deceased Sree Ram Krishna Nath." The Mortgage Registers (Alamot serial No. 6) contain volumes of transactions with several pages in five volumes of five years. Though 234 persons took loan mortgaging their ornaments, there is no direction regarding realization of interest accrued against the amount of money advanced to those 46 claimants and others starting from the time of taking loan by mortgaging their gold ornaments till the date of payment of the loans along with the accrued interest. The particulars of the loan advanced to each of 234 Mortgagors against the money advanced and the interest accrued have been clearly stated in the Mortgagor Registers (alamot serial No. 6) as well as in the Ledger Accounts Book. The money advanced to each of the mortgagors along with the interest from the date of taking loan till payment and the value of seized gold as per present market value of one of the mortgagors has been worked out as an example in a separate price escalation sheet to find out the fluctuation of rate of money due from the mortgagors comparing the rise of price of gold ornaments. It is, therefore, not reasonable and justified if the claimants are allowed to receive their gold ornaments, the value of which has now increased more than 10 times by payment of money which they had taken as loan with accrued interest without comparing and taking into consideration the present market value of the gold ornaments. The aversions of the claimants that the mortgagors took loan by depositing gold ornaments, the value of which is more than four times than the money they received as loan is not correct at all. In fact, the mortgagors received loan from Ram Krishna Nath by depositing gold ornaments calculating the actual price and advancing 75% money of the market price of such gold ornaments as per list of Bangladesh Jewellery Samity. The disputed claims of the mortgagors should not and cannot be settled on the basis of record maintained in the Mortgage Registers (alamot serial No. 6) in view of the fact that the records maintained in the Registers do not include and reveal the transactions of all the claimants. The outstanding claim of the mortgagors can only be determined and settled from the Ledger Accounts Book maintained for this purpose for each transaction. Therefore, proper accounts of loan advanced to each claimant against deposited gold can only be determined from the Ledger Accounts Book along with the record maintained in the Mortgage Registers. The business in advancing loan by receiving gold ornaments as mortgage is carried on verbally as per the business practice and custom. There was no written document and there was no mortgage in writing as well. It is a prevalent business practice and custom that if the loan money along with the accrued interest is not repaid within 22(twenty two) to 30(thirty) months based on case to case starting from the date of taking loan, in that case, the loan advanced with accrued interest stands adjusted with the price of the gold ornaments deposited as security. The particulars and records of those loan advanced along with accrued interest which were not repaid within 22(twenty two) to 30(thirty) months starting from the date of taking loan and which stood adjusted with the price of the gold ornaments deposited by the mortgagors as security have been properly maintained in the Ledger Accounts Book. As such, the loans along with accrued interest which stood adjusted in the aforesaid manner are not tenable. There are instances in which cases two or more claimants used the same serial token number which will be shown from their own applications. As such, it is necessary to verify first each claimant's serial token number comparing the Mortgage Registers along with the Ledger Accounts Book so that no claimant can come up with fake claims. The total amount of gold ornaments seized and now lying in the custody of Bangladesh Bank is 104 (one hundred four) kgs, 4(four) bhoris and 4½ (four and half) rotis. Out of which, late Ram Krishna Nath was the owner of 820 bhoris, 7 annas and 7 rotis and the rest of the gold ornaments belong to 79 claimants and 155 mortgagors. These 79 claimants came up with the claims in the Court, but the rest 155 other mortgagors whose gold ornaments are also lying with Bangladesh Bank did not come up with any claim in the Court, but they are pursuing and pressing the petitioners to settle their account and to return their deposited gold. This has created a complicated legal position in view of the fact that this Division directed to return the gold and other articles to the claimants as per Mortgage Registers (alamot serial No. 6), but while passing the direction, it did not consider the seizure list as well as the Ledger Accounts Book. Thus, out of 104 (one hundred four) kgs, 4(four) bhoris and 4½ rotis of gold ornaments, the petitioners own and claim 820 bhoris, 7 annas and 7 rotis and silver ornaments weighing 3 kgs, 500 grams, silver stone worth of Taka 5,545 (taka five thousand, five hundred and forty five only) and cash money of Taka 23,45,325 (taka twenty three lakh, forty five thousand, three hundred and twenty five only), the balance gold ornaments belong to 155 mortgagors and 79 claimants. As such, if the direction of this Division is not modified in the light of the seizure list, the Mortgage Registers and the Ledger Accounts Book that would cause gross injustice to the petitioners, and any distribution of gold ornaments and other seized articles solely on the basis of the Mortgage Registers without considering the claims of the petitioners, all the claimants and the mortgagors would highly prejudice their lawful rights and this would tantamount to denial of justice to the petitioners. The money lending transactions carried out by Ram Krishna Nath was a continuous process with some of the mortgagors. In the process, some of the mortgagors used to take loan by depositing gold ornaments as security and they used to partly repay the money against their deposited gold and again availed loan against new mortgage. Out of such transaction, money recoverable from 80 claimants amounting to Taka 17,85,980 (Taka seventeen lakh, eighty five thousand, nine hundred and eighty only) as shown in the Ledger Accounts Book and typed separately remained unpaid. The particulars of the total claim of the petitioners as legal heirs and successors of late Sree Ram Krishna Nath are as below: 

 13. In view of the prayer made by the petitioners under Article 104 of the Constitution, we are to decide two questions: first, whether there is any illegality in the impugned order of the High Court Division calling for interference by this Court; second, whether, in the facts and circumstances of the case, the prayer made by the petitioners for doing complete justice made under Article 104 of the Constitution, deserves due consideration. 

 It is an admitted fact that the seized articles which include ornaments (both gold and silver), stone and cash money as cataloged in the seizure list (the seizure list has been filed with the additional paper book) were seized from the exclusive possession of Ram Krishna Nath since deceased from his Jewellery shop named "Nath Jewelers" having been raided by the District Task Force on 11-8-2004 giving rise to Kotwali Police Station Case No. 24 dated 12-8-2004 under section 25B of the Act, 1974 in which the Police submitted final report which was accepted by the Tribunal in Special Tribunal Case No.  108 of 2005 and accused Ram Krishna Nath was discharged from the case. In the context, it may be stated that in the police report (final report), it was clearly stated that during investigation, it was revealed that accused-Ram Krishna Nath, was a money lender and used to give loan against mortgaging of gold ornaments and he also used to deal in making, selling and purchasing gold ornaments; the accused and his fore-fathers had been doing business at the place of occurrence shop for over a long period. In the report, it was also specifically stated that cash money amounting to Taka 24,18,085.80 lying in deposit in the iron safe volt recovered by the informant was on account of daily business transactions. The Investigation Officer also sought direction upon the informant to return the four receipts issued by Bangladesh Bank for safe deposit of cash money along with other alamots to the accused. It further appears that before the Tribunal, prayer was made by accused-late Ram Krishna Nath to return him the seized ornaments, money and other materials, recovered from his shop. Subsequently 46 (forty six) persons as claimants also filed applications for return of the seized ornaments to them. The Tribunal while accepting the final report and discharging the accused from the case gave direction upon the concerned authorities to return the seized articles including the money to the principal accused-Ram Krishna Nath with a further direction upon him to give back the seized ornaments to the other claimants who deposited gold ornaments with him as per the seized Registers (Mortgage Registers). The Tribunal further directed the concerned Jimmader to return the seized ornaments and cash money to the accused and communicated the copy of the order to the Officer-in-charge, Kotwali Police Station, Chittagong Metropolitan Police and the Manager, Bangladesh Bank for information and for taking necessary steps. It is also a fact that the same informant, Subader Md Harun Mia of Kotwali Police Station Case No. 24 dated 12-8-2004 (giving rising to Special Tribunal Case No.  108 of 2007) lodged another FIR on 7-6-2005 against late Ram Krishna Nath as the sole accused giving rise to GR Case No. 393 of 2005 (arising out of Kotwali Police Station Case No.  16(6)2005) under section 13 of the Ain, 2002 and on an application filed by the Investigation Officer on 9-6-2005 alamots seized in connection with Kotwali Police Station Case No. 24(8)04 were shown as alamots in the latter case, i.e. Kotwali Police Station Case No. 16 (6)2005 and to keep the alamots in safe custody till disposal of the case. In the second case after investigation, the Police submitted charge-sheet. Challenging the proceedings, the application for quashment was filed before the High Court Division and the proceedings were quashed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 4296 of 2006 giving rise to Criminal Appeal No. 43 of 2009. 

 16. The High Court Division quashed the proceedings of GR Case No. 393 of 2005 (corresponding to Kotwali Police Station Case No.  16 (6)2005) on the clear finding: 

 (The High Court Division relied upon the case of Abdul Quader vs State, 28 DLR (AD) 38 and an unreported case, Tozammel Hoque and another, Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.  6609 of 2003) The High Court Division gave the further finding: 

 "More so it is revealed in the investigation of the first case (Kotwali PS Case No. 24(8)2004) arising out of the same occurrence that money recovered from the Volt of the iron safe of Nath Jewellers is on account of daily transaction." 

 17. The High Court Division further held that the charge-sheet submitted by the Police in the second case accusing the petitioner on the self-same occurrence was "malicious, calculated to victimize and harass the accused petitioner and further proceeding in the case" would be an abuse of the process of the Court. 

 18. As already stated hereinbefore, in the first case being Kotwali Police Station Case No. 24 dated 12-8-2004 (GR Number is not available from the record), the Police submitted final report which was accepted by the Tribunal and accused-Ram Krishna Nath since deceased was discharged from the case. The second case being GR Case No. 393 of 2005 corresponding to Kotwali Police Station Case No.  16(6)2005 was quashed by the High Court Division on the findings, inter alia, as quoted and noted down hereinbefore. The order of the High Court Division quashing the proceedings has been maintained by this Division (Criminal Appeal No. 43 of 2009). And the present leave petition is not in respect of the said quashed proceedings, but is an off-shoot originating from the order passed by the Tribunal in Special Tribunal Case No. 108 of 2005 as affirmed by this Division in Criminal Appeal No. 43 of 2009. It is also necessary to state that the order of the Tribunal accepting the final report and discharging the accused from the case with the direction to return the seized articles and money to accused-Ram Krishna Nath with further direction upon him to return the seized ornaments to the claimants who deposited those with him as per the seized Registers were not challenged by either parties. However, since the articles seized in the first case being Kotwali Police State Case No. 24 dated 12-8-2004 were shown as alamots in the second case, i.e. GR Case No. 393 of 2005 and in the meantime, the principal accused Ram Krishna Nath died while dismissing the appeal (the appeal arose out of GR Case No. 393 of 2005) direction of the High Court Division was modified to the effect as quoted hereinbefore. In fact, the direction given by the High Court Division as modified by this Court in the appeal was nothing but endorsement of the order passed by the Tribunal in Special Tribunal Case No. 108 of 2005. 

 19. Now a pertinent follow up question arises as to whether the Tribunal was legally correct to give the direction upon accused-late Ram Krishna Nath to return the seized ornaments to the other claimants who deposited those with him as per the seized Registers and report compliance thereof to it within 1(one) month. To answer the question, we need to see the provisions of section 517 of the Code. Admittedly, the ornaments (both gold and silver), cash money and the other articles as evident from the seizure list were seized in connection with Kotwali Police Station Case No. 24 dated 12-8-2004. Section 517 of the Code deals with the disposal of the property seized during investigation. This section is in Chapter XLIII of the property seized during investigation. This section is in Chapter XLIII of the Code. The heading of the Chapter is "OF THE DISPOSAL OF PROPERTY." In this Chapter, there are 10(ten) sections: 516A-525; of these 10(ten) sections, section 517 is relevant. In the context, it may be stated that in the Act, 1974, there is no provision as to how the property seized in connection with a case under the Act, 1974 or alamots of a case under the Act, 1974, shall be disposed of in case of conclusion of a trial or in a case which ends with the acceptance of a final report and discharge of the accused. However, section 29 of the Act, 1974 has provided that the provisions of the Code, so far as they are not inconsistent with the provisions of the Act, shall apply to the proceedings of the Special Tribunals, and such Special Tribunals shall have all the powers conferred by the Code as a Court of Sessions exercising original jurisdiction. It may further be stated that the Act, 1974 has provided the Tribunals with the power to pass necessary orders in case of confiscation of the property at the time of disposal of the case either in the form of acquittal or conviction, but it has not provided the Tribunals with any power to deal with any seized property or alamots after the disposal of the case. That being the position of the Act, 1974, the Tribunals cannot be left without any power to deal with such matter and so the legislature advisedly incorporated section 29 in the Act, 1974 as discussed herein-above. So the Tribunal has the power to pass necessary order for disposal of the properly seized during investigation or alamots in a case under the Act, 1974 invoking the aid of section 517 of the Code and in the instant case, the seized articles were definitely seized as it appeared to the law enforcing agencies that an offence appeared to have been committed because of the possession of the articles by accused-Ram Krishna Nath as contemplated in section 517 of the Code. Here, as found earlier in the first case, the police submitted final report and the Tribunal having accepted the final report discharged accused-Ram Krishna Nath from the case and in the second case, though charge-sheet was submitted by the Police, the proceedings were quashed by the High Court Division on the clear finding that the allegations made in the FIR even taken to be true did not constitute any offence under section 25B of the Act, 1974 or under section 13 of the Ain, 2002 or under any law of the land and that the charge-sheet submitted by the police accusing Ram Krishna Nath was malicious, calculated to victimize and harass him. That being the admitted factual and legal position, accused late Ram Krishna Nath was entitled to get return of the articles seized from him and the Tribunal was obliged to pass necessary order in that respect in exercise of its power under section 517 of the Code. It may be stated that the seizure list prima-facie shows that all the articles which include ornaments (both gold and silver), stone and cash money were seized from the exclusive possession of late Ram Krishna Nath from his shop Nath Jewellers and none else and there is no dispute as well in that respect. 

 20. Admittedly, 46 (forty six) claimants who applied to the Tribunal as well as before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (by now the number has been increased to 79 as stated in the better statement) took loan from late Ram Krishna Nath by mortgaging their ornaments to him, so they cannot deny or escape from the liabilities with which they are saddled against the mortgage created by them. 46 (forty six) claimants who applied before the Tribunal to return the gold ornaments to them and also before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong clearly admitted the said fact of creation of mortgage by them by depositing gold ornaments to late Ram Krishna Nath. In the application filed by 46 (forty six) claimants before this Court for adding them as respondents in the leave petition, they have simply stated that they are the claimants of the seized gold, silver ornaments and the other articles and they have not denied the fact that they took loan from late Ram Krishna Nath by mortgaging their ornaments as security. On their behalf an additional paper book has been filed. In the additional paper book as many as 29 applications which were filed before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong in Kotwali Police Station Case No.  24(8)2004 for returning gold ornaments to them have been incorporated. In those applications also the respective claimant clearly admitted the fact of taking loan from late Ram Krishna Nath by mortgaging their ornaments. In the applications, the respective claimant also admitted the fact that late Ram Krishna Nath was a licensed Money Lender and he used to give loan against the mortgage of gold ornaments. 

 21. At the risk of repetition, it is stated that in the better statement, it has been categorically stated that the gold ornaments which were seized from lockers: A, B, C and D of Nath Jewellers contained in different packets with the name of the mortgagors, serial numbers, amount of gold deposited and the amount of money taken as loan with dates. Though 234 persons took loan by mortgaging their ornaments, there is no direction regarding realization of interest accrued against the amount of money advanced to them including 46 claimants starting from the time of taking loan by mortgaging their gold ornaments till the date of the payment of loans along with the accrued interest. The particulars of the loan advanced to each of the 234 mortgagors against the money advanced and the interest accrued thereon have been clearly stated in the Mortgage Registers (Alamot serial No. 6) as well as in the Ledger Accounts Book. The disputed claims of the mortgagors should not and cannot be settled on the basis of the records maintained in the Mortgage Registers in view of the fact that the records maintained in the Registers do not include and reveal the transactions of all the claimants. The outstanding claim of the mortgagors can only be determined and settled from the Ledger Accounts Book maintained for this purpose for such transactions. Therefore, proper accounts of loan advanced to each claimant against deposited gold can only be determined from the Ledger Accounts Book along with the records maintained in the Mortgage Registers. It has further been stated that the business in advancing loan by receiving gold ornaments as mortgage is carried out verbally as per business practice and custom. There is no written document, and there is no mortgage in writing as well. It was a prevalent business practice and custom that, if the loan money along with the accrued interest was not repaid within 22(twenty two) to 30(thirty) months starting from the date of taking loan, in that case, the loan advanced with accrued interest would stand adjusted with the price of the gold ornaments deposited as security. The particulars and records of those loan advanced along with accrued interest, which were not repaid within 22(twenty two) to 30(thirty) months starting from the date of taking loan and which stood adjusted with the price of gold ornaments deposited by the mortgagors as security have been properly maintained in the Ledger Accounts Book. The loans along with accrued interest which stood adjusted in the aforesaid manner are not tenable. There are instances in which cases two or more claimants used the same serial token number which will be showed from their own application. As such, it is necessary to verify first each claimant's serial token number comparing with the Mortgage Registers along with the Ledger Accounts Book so that no claimant can come up with fake claims. 

 22. The above broad pertinent facts stated in the better statement have neither been denied nor controverted by 46 (forty six) claimants by filing any affidavit or counter statements in any form, rather some of those have been admitted in the applications filed before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate as incorporated in the additional paper book. But it is a fact that the above facts were not earlier stated either before the Tribunal or before the High Court Division or before this Court and consequently, neither the Tribunal nor the High Court Division nor this Court could consider those facts in giving the necessary direction as to the disposal of the seized articles while accepting the final report, disposing the quashing application and dismissing Criminal Appeal No. 43 of 2009 respectively. Be that as it may, since the above facts have not been denied by 46 (forty six) claimants rather have been admitted in the applications filed before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong for returning their gold ornaments and those are quite in conformity with the facts as revealed during the investigation of the first case (Kotwali Police Station Case No. 24 dated 12.08.2004), the seizure list, the Mortgage Registers and the Ledger Accounts Book, we cannot just ignore them and we consider it proper to take judicial notice thereof to decide as to whether we should exercise the power vested in this Court under article 104 of the Constitution. From the above, it is prima facie clear the relationship of mortgagors and mortgagee between late Ram Krishna Nath and 46 (forty six) claimants and the other mortgagors existed at the time of seizure of the ornaments along with other articles. Admittedly, late Ram Krishna Nath was a licensed Money Lender and he used to do his money lending business on accepting gold ornaments as security as per the prevalent practice and custom, besides being in the business of making and selling gold ornaments. Therefore, the leave petitioners who are his legal heirs were/are entitled to get the interest accrued against the amount of loan advanced to 46 (forty six) claimants and others starting from the time of taking such loan along with the loan money till the date of the repayment of such loan, but no direction regarding realization of interest from 46 claimants and the other mortgagors which accrued against the amount of loan money advanced to them was given either by the Tribunal or by the High Court Division or by this Court. 

 24. In the background of the case as discussed above, it appears to us reasonable, legal, practical and consciousable that the individual case of each of 46 (forty six) claimants and the other mortgagors be examined with reference to 3(three) documents, namely: the Seizure list, the Mortgage Registers and the Ledger Accounts Book in order to settle the claim arising out of the loan availed by them by depositing their gold ornaments as security with late Ram Krishna Nath. Therefore, we find merit in the contention raised by the petitioners in the better statement that if the direction of this Court "is not modified in the light of the seizure list (Annexure-I), the Mortgage Register (Alamot Serial No. 6) and Ledger Account Book (Annexure-J) there will cause gross injustice to the petitioners and any distribution of gold ornaments and other seized articles solely on the basis of Mortgage Registers (Alamot serial No.  6) without considering the claims of the petitioners and all claimants and the Mortgagors would highly prejudice their lawful rights and this would tantamount to denial of justice" to them. Our further considered view is that 46 (forty six) claimant mortgagors and the other mortgagors cannot get back their gold ornaments and the other articles just paying the loan money taken by them on the basis of the Mortgage Registers without meeting their other liabilities, such as, payment of interest that accrued over the years against the loan availed by them, the adjustment of the loan money and the interest accrued thereon with the price of the ornaments mortgaged due to the non-refund of the loan money along with the interest arising out of the transaction as per the prevalent practice and custom. But in the appeal, it was simply directed that "the seized gold, silver ornament, cash money and other articles which have been deposited with Bangladesh Bank are to be returned to their rightful owners namely 46 claimants and other mortgagors in accordance with the record maintained in the Registers (Alamot Serial No.  6)." It is true that this Court also gave direction upon the Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong to the effect "to hear the claims of the individual claimants named in the Registers (Alamot serial No. 6) and to return their ornaments upon realizing the money, if any, is due to Nath Jewellers to which the Jewellery had been mortgaged. And money so realized is to be handed over to the rightful heirs and successor in the business of Sree Ram Krishna Nath." But these directions do not cover all the liabilities of the mortgagors that might have saddled them including 46 (forty six) claimants as discussed above. And if the directions of this Court given in Criminal Appeal No. 43 of 2009 remain, the leave petitioners who are the legal heirs of Ram Krisha Nath shall be deprived of their legitimate dues from the mortgagors including 46 claimants and the other rights arising out of the transactions as per the prevalent practice and custom of money lending business which have been reflected /recorded in the Ledger Accounts Book as pointed out hereinbefore and that shall be to the great detriment to the interest and vested right of the leave petitioners and would give an unjust financial benefit to the claimants and the other mortgagors and all these justify the prayer of the petitioners to exercise the power vested in this Court under Article 104 of the Constitution. It is also a fact that from the date of seizure of the articles cataloged in the seizure list (seizure was made on 11-8-2004) by now more than 9(nine) years elapsed and the petitioners being the legal heirs of late Ram Krishna Nath, they cannot afford to suffer further. 

 25. In the context, we may refer to the case of M/s Gannysons Ltd vs Sonali Bank, 37 DLR (AD) 42. In that case, this Division invoked the power vested in it under article 104 of the Constitution to do complete justice on the following facts: 

 "Sonali Bank, respondent No. 1, obtained a decree in Title Suit No. 249 of 1976 for foreclosure and sale of the mortgaged properties belonging to the appellant company and put it into execution in Title Execution No. 46 of 1980. Appellant-company appeared before the Court and prayed for staying the execution of the decree on the grounds that since the Bank proceeded against the appellant Company's properties being treated as abandoned by the Government, the Directors of the appellant Company were not properly served with notice and that had, therefore, no knowledge of the aforesaid title suit. As a result they did not appear in the suit. Also the Government which was made a party did not take any steps. However, on the prayer of the appellant Company the proceeding in the execution case was stayed till October 20, 1981. In Writ Petition No. 720 of 1981 a Rule was issued at the instance of the appellant company on October 20, 1981. But it abated on 24 March 1982 after the proclamation of Martial Law. In Miscellaneous Case No. 958 of 1981 which was filed by the appellant Company under section 47 of the Code its prayer against the execution of the decree obtained in Title Suit No. 249 of 1976 was disallowed by the Court. The appellant Company's appeal against this order was dismissed by the High Court Division on 9 November 1982. The appellant Company, being aggrieved, moved this Court and succeeded in having the appeal (Civil Appeal No. 43 of 1983) against the order of the trial Court rejecting their objection under section 47 of the Code allowed. Appellants filed review petition against the judgment passed in the civil appeal against the concluding paragraph of the judgment which was as follows: 

 "Decree dated 27-3-80 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 249 of 1976 be stayed for six months and the Miscellaneous Case No. 958 of 1981 pending in the 3rd court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Dhaka be struck down." 

 "For that consistently with the reasoning’s in the main body of the judgment and the decision allowing the appeal (CA No. 43 of 1983) arising out of Miscellaneous Case No. 958 of 1981 started under section 47 CPC (at the instance of M/s Gannysons Ltd. and another) the Title Execution Case No. 46 of 1980 pending in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka, needs to be struck down and the said Miscellaneous Case No. 958 of 1981 of the same court allowed and that the order saying the decree dated 27-3-80 in Title Suit No. 279 of 1976 of the 3rd Court of the Subordinate Judge needs to be deleted." 

 27. Considering the definition of abandoned property as given in President's Order No. 16 of 1972, it was found that Gannysons Limited Company, in no circumstances, could be declared as an abandoned property, allowed the review application, declared that the property was not an abandoned property, struck down the execution case subject to payment of the decretal amount to the Bank directly by the appellants and directed the Government to release the property treating Title Suit No.  508 of 1982 filed by the appellant as withdrawn being infructuous. In that case, Fazle Munim, CJ observed: 

 "17. In view of the circumstances above and in virtue of the power conferred upon this Court by the Constitution of Bangladesh, vide Article 104, to do complete justice in a case it is declared that Gannyasons Limited is not an abandoned property, it should, therefore, be immediately, released. Along with the release of Gannysons Limited any of its properties, assests and capital should also be released and returned to it." 

 28. In the above backdrop, we consider it a fit case to exercise the power vested in this Court under article 104 of the Constitution for doing complete justice in the matter by modifying the directions given by the Tribunal, the High Court Division and this Court in Criminal Appeal No. 43 of 2009. 

 (a)	The informant is directed to return the original receipts of safe deposit of the seized articles and the money deposited with Bangladesh Bank to the present petitioners who are the legal heirs of deceased accused-Ram Krishna Nath of the case. The Commander of 43 Rifle Battalion, Halisahar, Chittagong as the recipient of original receipt of Bangladesh Bank in respect of the seized articles is directed to ensure return of original safe deposit to the Joint Manager, Banking (Bangladesh Bank), Chittagong Branch. The seized articles (gold and silver ornaments, cash money, stones) lying in safe deposit in the custody of Bangladesh Bank, Chittagong Branch, be released and handed over to the present petitioners after receiving the original receipts from the Commander, 43, Rifle Battalion, Hali Sahar, Chittagong. 

 (c)	the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong shall also look into the claim of the present petitioners (who are the legal heirs of late Ram Krishna Nath) that in some cases the price of the seized gold, silver ornaments and other articles already stood adjusted with the loan money and the interest accrued thereon due to the non-payment of the loan money along with the interest accrued thereon by the mortgagors within 22 (twenty two) to 30 (thirty) months from the date of taking the loan as per the prevalent business practice and custom in advancing loan by receiving gold, silver ornaments and other articles as mortgage. In considering the above claim of the petitioners as well as the claim of the individual claimant/mortgagor including the 46 claimants to get return of their mortgaged gold, silver ornaments and other articles, the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate shall consider the Mortgage Registers and the Ledger Accounts Book along with the seizure list; 

 The directions given by the Metropolitan Special Tribunal No. 1, Chittagong in Special Tribunal Case No. 108 of 2005, by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 4296 of 2006 and by this Court in Criminal Appeal No. 43 of 2009 stand accordingly.
